body.statement: For every observed mass array \(q\) and budget pair \((\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B\), the projection of all laws \(P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\) inducing \(q\) onto \((d,h,n)\) is exactly \(\bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\). Every point of every branch \(Q_o\) lifts to a full response law inducing the same \(q\), with the displayed \(h_x\) and \(n_x\). Each branch admits a rational extended formulation with \(O(mK)\) variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it converts a nonconvex full response-law problem into exact linear-size branches without losing any compatible law or projected point.
body.gap: Dong and Heiler maintain treatment monotonicity and within-cell one-sided selection for a mean target, Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen omit post-treatment selection, and Bartalotti, Kédagni, and Possebom use latent-index treatment selection and a monotone-selection refinement that exclude, respectively, treatment defiers and within-cell opposing selection responses. None contains this joint projection or reverse lift.
body.consumer: It makes the survivor-complier ordinal-benefit robustness surface exactly computable for the Job Corps and Oregon encouragement designs.
